title: Resolved strict quotient pullback with its specified augmentation
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism and $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_{T'}$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}A_T}A_{T'}$ be the module pullback along the projection-defined coefficient map [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $Q,Q'$ for the source and target strict-tower derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a universal total left-derived pair $(\widetilde L,\tau)$ for levelwise $G$, computed on the objectwise K-flat flat-term class [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements].
For a K-flat flat-term complex $P$ of $A_T$-modules, put $R(P)_n=P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, with transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$, and let $a_P:\Delta P\to R(P)$ be $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For any objectwise K-flat flat-term strict resolution $r:H_\bullet\to R(P)$, the counit formula
$$\chi_r=\tau_{H_\bullet}\,\widetilde L(Qr)^{-1}:\widetilde L(QR(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'G(H_\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism. The augmentation induced after derived pullback is the natural morphism
$$w_P=\widetilde L(Qa_P)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}:Q'G(\Delta P)\longrightarrow\widetilde L(QR(P)),$$
with $G(\Delta P)=\Delta G(P)$. It satisfies $Q'G(r)\chi_rw_P=Q'G(a_P)$. For another such resolution $s:H'_\bullet\to R(P)$ the canonical comparison $\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$ identifies $\chi_rw_P$ with $\chi_sw_P$; these comparisons satisfy the three-resolution cocycle. The maps $w_P$ are natural in maps of K-flat flat-term $P$, and compatible with localization at quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives. No lift of $a_P$ to $H_\bullet$ and no K-flatness of the quotient levels $R(P)_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing completed pullback exactness proved in CompletedTowerPullback: its projection-defined coefficient map equals the integral coefficient isomorphism of the datum. The exact ordinary tower functor has the termwise derived localization and invertible comparison. The private exactPullbackCounit_isIso theorem transfers this invertibility by uniqueness to the arbitrary specified universal pair LF,tau. Its actual cochain counit is a composite with quotient-comparison isomorphisms, hence invertible. Set delta to this counit on the constant tower. Use completedPullbackConstantComplex_eq for the asserted equality of strict complexes.

proof.text: Set chi_r to the inverse of LF(Qr) followed by the actual cochain counit on H. The denominator is invertible because r is a quasi-isomorphism. Construct the cochain counit natural transformation by whiskering tau with the existing quotient comparisons; its naturality at r identifies chi_r followed by QG(r) with the counit at R(P). Naturality at the actual augmentation then gives the augmented resolution identity. No lift of the augmentation or K-flatness of quotient levels is used.

proof.text: The comparisons are chi_r inverse followed by chi_s. Associativity and the inverse identities give compatibility with the augmented arrows, the cocycle, and the identity comparison. Naturality of the actual strict coefficient augmentation, together with cochain counit naturality on constant complexes and cancellation of delta, gives w_P D(f) = B(f) w_Pprime.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f of K-flat representatives, reuse the existing reductionChange_quasiIso theorem at each quotient coefficient and exact restriction of scalars. The existing level_complex_eq identifies these with the evaluations of R(f); quasiIso_iff_evaluation yields a tower quasi-isomorphism. Thus D(f) is invertible. Exact completed tower pullback and exact constant towers make B(f) invertible. Multiplying the naturality equation by their inverses gives the required inverse square.
